title: Kickout Flashing at the Sidewall
description: Kickout flashing is the metal turn where a Houston roof meets a sidewall. It sends rain into the gutter instead of letting it run behind the siding.
html:
A sidewall leak rarely starts in the middle of a shingle. It starts at the bottom corner, where the roof stops and the wall keeps going. That corner needs a small piece of bent metal, a kickout, to throw water into the gutter. Miss it, and every Houston downpour runs behind the siding.

What the piece actually does

Step flashing is a separate piece of metal on each shingle course where the roof meets the wall. The siding or counterflashing laps over it. The last piece, at the eave, has to turn outward. That turn is the kickout. Water coming down the wall-to-roof joint hits the turn and dumps into the gutter instead of continuing down the wall.

Without the turn, water follows the flashing to the end and slips behind the trim. It wets the wall sheathing, the stud bay, and eventually the interior at the baseboard, often a room away from the corner you can see from the yard. People caulk the bottom of the siding. The caulk holds for a season. The joint behind it does not.

How we can tell from the ground

Look at the bottom of any roof-to-wall intersection. You should see metal sticking out past the siding and aimed at the gutter, not buried in a bead of sealant. Stains on the siding below that corner, soft trim, or a gutter that stops short of the wall are the usual companions. On two-story houses the same corner is just harder to see, and the water has a longer wall to travel.

A kickout by itself does not fix step flashing that was never installed, or siding nailed through the metal. We open enough of the corner to see the courses, replace what is missing, and put the kickout where the water already wants to go. If the sheathing is soft, that is a wall repair, and we say so before we close it back up.

This is a roof repair, not a reason to replace the field, unless the shingles at that wall are already done. If the stain is at a sidewall corner, start there. Request a free inspection or call (281) 541-0027.
